name: Crucible ArcShield Welding Gauntlet
description:
Heavy-duty split-leather shell with aluminized dorsal panels and a dense aramid lining, built for sustained arc flash and slag exposure. Stitching is triple-locked with heat-resistant thread; the cuff extends mid-forearm and fastens with a single reinforced snap. Color is a mottled ochre-brown with scorch marks that accumulate as a badge of use.

The right gauntlet ships with a chrome-arm cuff adapter ring, allowing wearers with augmented forearms to snap the gauntlet directly onto a prosthetic wrist collar. The left features a pull-tab quick-release for emergencies.
functionality: Rated to 1,200°C radiant flash. Aug-compatible cuff adapter accommodates standard prosthetic wrist collars. Quick-release left cuff allows single-hand doffing. Reinforced palm patch resists puncture from metal burrs and slag splash.
what_it_says: This person works the real fire — no simulators, no delegating.
story_hooks: A pair found in a Shelf squat still has the previous owner's name stamped inside — and she's on a missing persons board.
The chrome-arm adapter ring is a known fit for a banned military prosthetic model, raising questions about where Crucible's specs came from.
A welder uses the gauntlets to smuggle data chips in the cuff cavity — the aluminized layer masks scanner reads.
